title: Probate Attorney Hourly Rates and Fees in 2026
summary: Learn about probate attorney hourly rates, total costs, and what drives fees up in July 2026.
body_text: In general, probate attorney fees in 2026 range from $150 to $400 per hour for an estate. Some states set fees by statute, based on the gross value of the estate. Others leave fees open to negotiation. What you pay depends on different factors, including where the estate is, how complex it is, and which billing structure an attorney uses. Several factors can lead to attorney fees being higher than the baseline rate. Examples of this may include: contested wills and family disputes requiring court appearances and additional legal work. Or, estates with real property in more than one state having to open a separate ancillary probate proceeding in each state, which means additional filings and attorney time. For context, attorney fees are paid from estate assets, not from any beneficiary's personal funds. The executor draws on the estate account to cover legal costs before making distributions to heirs. In statutory fee states, the attorney fee amount is calculated from the gross estate value, which includes the full market value of real property before subtracting any mortgage balance. Key Takeaways: In general, probate attorney fees in 2026 range from $150 to $400 per hour. California and Florida set fees by statute based on gross estate value; a $500,000 California estate will have roughly $13,000 in attorney fees. Contested wills, out-of-state property, and missing documents can lead to increased costs. Attorney fees are paid from estate assets before distributions. Elayne works alongside attorneys, managing administrative tasks like account searches and institutional notifications. How Probate Attorneys Help A probate attorney guides an estate through the court-supervised process of validating a will, paying debts, and transferring assets to beneficiaries. Their work spans across several distinct areas: Preparing and filing the petition to open probate with the court, along with the death certificate , original will, and any supporting documents the jurisdiction requires Notifying creditors and beneficiaries within court-mandated deadlines, which vary by state Identifying, valuing, and inventorying estate assets, including real property, financial accounts, and personal property Handling creditor claims, reviewing which debts are valid, and overseeing payment from estate funds Preparing and filing any required estate tax returns at the state or federal level Drafting the final accounting and distribution plan, then securing court approval before assets transfer to beneficiaries Some attorneys take on a limited role, advising the executor on specific steps while the executor handles filings directly. Others manage the process end to end, appearing in court and corresponding with financial institutions on the estate's behalf. {{blog-cta-legal}} Fee Structures Probate Attorneys Use Hourly Billing Most attorneys bill by the hour, with rates that vary based on geography, experience, and estate complexity. Straightforward estates in lower-cost states may receive rates in the range of $150 to $250 per hour, while attorneys in major metro areas or those handling contested matters may charge $300 to $500 or more. Percentage-Based Fees Some states permit attorneys to charge a percentage of the gross estate value. California and Florida, for example, set statutory fee schedules that define what attorneys may collect based on estate size. Flat Fees For routine, uncontested probates, some attorneys offer a flat fee covering the full proceeding. This gives families cost predictability, though the scope of what is included varies. Statutory Fee States How California's Statutory Fee Schedule Works California Probate Code sections 10800 and 10810 set fees for both the executor and the attorney on a sliding scale tied to the gross estate value: Gross Estate Value Attorney Fee Rate First $100,000 4% Next $100,000 3% Next $800,000 2% Next $9,000,000 1% Next $15,000,000 0.5% Above $25,000,000 Court discretion How Florida's Statutory Fee Schedule Works Florida sets fees under Fla. Stat. § 733.6171 on a percentage basis tied to gross estate value: 3% on the first $40,000, 2.5% on the next $60,000, and 3% on amounts above $100,000. Estates above $3,000,000 are subject to negotiated or court-set fees. Gross Estate Value Attorney Fee Rate First $40,000 3% Next $60,000 2.5% Above $100,000 3% Above $3,000,000 Negotiated or court-set Florida also allows fees for "extraordinary services," which function similarly to California's add-on provisions, and uses gross estate value as the basis for calculation, not the net value after debts or mortgages. Both states use gross estate value, not net value, as the basis for calculation. Probate Attorney Cost Comparison by State Probate attorney costs vary considerably from state to state, shaped by local court fees, attorney fee structures, and how each state's probate laws govern compensation. Some states set statutory fees for probate attorneys, meaning the law defines exactly what an attorney can charge based on a percentage of the estate's gross value. Other states leave fees entirely to negotiation between the attorney and the estate. Statutory Fee States vs. Negotiated Fee States In statutory fee states, attorney compensation follows a fixed schedule. California, for example, sets fees at 4% of the first $100,000, 3% of the next $100,000, 2% of the next $800,000, and so on. Florida uses a similar percentage-based structure. In negotiated fee states, hourly rates and flat fees are common. Rates in these states typically range from $150 to $350 per hour, though complex estates in high-cost markets can push rates well above that. Beyond Attorney Fees: Other Probate Costs Probate costs including court filing fees are typically $200 to $500, varying by state and county. Executor compensation falls between 1% to 5% of the estate under most state laws, though family members frequently waive this. Professional appraisals are required for real property, business interests, and certain personal property to determine date-of-death values. Surety bond premiums range from $500 to $1,500 annually unless the will explicitly waives the requirement. Accountant fees cover the final personal income return and any estate income tax filings. {{blog-cta-legal}} Who Pays Probate Attorney Fees Fees are paid from estate assets in most states, not from the executor's or any beneficiary's personal accounts. The executor draws on estate funds to cover legal costs before distributions go to heirs. How Elayne Supports Families and Legal Teams Elayne supports families and legal teams by handling estate administration tasks : searching for accounts and assets, notifying financial institutions, and helping coordinate the administrative steps that follow a death. What Elayne Handles Elayne searches for financial accounts, insurance policies, real property records, unclaimed assets, and eligible survivor benefits through its Verified Asset Search. The search runs across databases, document records, and financial records to surface accounts and assets that might otherwise be missed. Once accounts are identified, Elayne notifies financial institutions directly. This includes banks, brokerage firms, and retirement account custodians, each of which has its own documentation requirements and timelines. Elayne also scans financial records for recurring charges: streaming subscriptions, gym memberships, software plans, and other accounts. Elayne manages cancellation with each provider directly and monitors subsequent statements to confirm charges have stopped. A Shared View of the Estate Elayne's shared dashboard gives authorized family members, co-executors, and attorneys access to documents, account records, and progress tracking in one place. For dual-role executors who serve as both executor and beneficiary, the dashboard also functions as a documented record of decisions made. FAQs What is the average cost of working with a probate attorney in 2026, and what does the service include? Most probate attorneys charge between $150 and $400 per hour in 2026, with total fees for a straightforward estate typically falling in the $3,000 to $15,000 range. A straightforward estate generally means one with a clear will, a modest number of assets, no disputes among heirs, and no real property in more than one state. That figure covers court filings, creditor notification, asset inventory, and the final distribution accounting. Contested matters, out-of-state property, or tax complications can push total costs well above the range referenced above, sometimes into $20,000 to $30,000 territory or higher for large or complex estates. Are probate attorney fees negotiable? In states that don't set fees by statute, rates and billing structures are open to discussion. Flat fees, limited-scope arrangements, and hybrid models can be discussed during an initial consultation. In statutory fee states, the schedule is set by law, though extraordinary fee add-ons may have some room for negotiation. How do California and Florida probate attorney fees compare to negotiated-fee states like Texas or New York? California and Florida set attorney fees by statute as a percentage of the gross estate value, so a $500,000 estate in California amounts to roughly $13,000 in attorney fees before any extraordinary charges. Texas and New York leave fees to negotiation, where hourly rates of $150 to $350 are typical. What drives probate attorney fees higher than the baseline hourly rate? Contested wills, family disputes, and estates with out-of-state real property are common reasons for increased costs. Who pays probate attorney fees? body_text: DALLAS (July 13, 2026) — AECOM (NYSE: ACM), the trusted global infrastructure leader, today announced it has been selected as Independent Certifier for the design and construction of The Wave – Stage 1, with joint venture partner Bureau Veritas. As Queensland’s next major rail project, The Wave will enhance regional connectivity, reduce road congestion, improve accessibility, and support population growth as part of the 2032 Delivery Plan for the Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games. For the next six years, the joint venture will certify the design and construction of a new dual-track rail line from Beerwah to Caloundra that includes new and upgraded stations along the line. Through this work, the joint venture will ensure the project meets its safety, operational and regulatory objectives. “The Wave represents a transformative step forward for South East Queensland, connecting the eastern communities of the Sunshine Coast to the passenger rail network and making travel simpler for thousands of residents across the region,” said Mark McManamny, chief executive of AECOM’s Australia and New Zealand region. “As Independent Certifier, we are focused on giving the Queensland Government, communities and future users confidence that the project meets the standards expected of infrastructure that will serve the region for generations.” AECOM brings deep, multidisciplinary expertise across rail, transport and major infrastructure, with a proven track record of delivering Independent Assurance on some of Australia’s most complex and high-profile projects, including Melbourne Metro Tunnel, Sydney Metro Brownfields and the M1 Pacific Motorway extension to Raymond Terrace. “We continue to win premier roles on a robust pipeline of major transportation opportunities in Australia,” said Russell Jackson, interim chief executive of AECOM’s global Transportation business. “Our advantage is the result of decades-long investment in trusted, local teams backed by the technical knowledge of the #1 Transportation design firm in the world, as ranked by Engineering-News Record . We’re proud to support Australia’s federal, state and local governments as they continue to prioritize transportation modernization and capacity upgrades, particularly ahead of the Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games.” The Wave is a key component of the Queensland Government’s 2032 Delivery Plan and infrastructure program for the Games. Beyond the Games, the project is expected to strengthen regional connectivity across the Sunshine Coast, improving access to employment hubs, social infrastructure and tourist destinations throughout the region. title: A Gambler 500 Mea Culpa
summary: In a vacant grass lot behind the Jefferson County Sheriff’s Office, a second-gen Honda CR-V revs its engine in the afternoon sun. The ear-splitting tones easily crack 115 decibels. Wha-POW, wha-POW, wha-POW, wha-POW! The 2.4-liter four-banger pops off the rev limiter, its straight-piped exhaust protruding through a few holes haphazardly cut into the hood. The racket […]
body_text: In a vacant grass lot behind the Jefferson County Sheriff’s Office, a second-gen Honda CR-V revs its engine in the afternoon sun. The ear-splitting tones easily crack 115 decibels. Wha-POW, wha-POW, wha-POW, wha-POW! The 2.4-liter four-banger pops off the rev limiter, its straight-piped exhaust protruding through a few holes haphazardly cut into the hood. The racket echoes off a half dozen hulking roll-off dumpsters surrounding it, amplifying it for the unfortunate bystanders. “F*@# that guy,” Tate Morgan, the founder of the Gambler 500 , says with a chuckle. “I had to talk to him six or seven times yesterday.” Directly in front of Morgan and me is a black John Deere backhoe, its operator gleefully tearing apart an abandoned trailer that had been dragged off public land here into Gambler Town to be disposed of. The black claws tear indiscriminate chunks of the roof and walls and effortlessly toss them into one of the dumpsters. The previous occupants’ belongings spill out onto the ground—bedding, clothing, a child’s toy truck. “It’s good we’re down wind of that,” Morgan nods toward the quickly disappearing trailer. Nick Jaynes Though Morgan rolled up to me on an aging scooter designed for Japanese commuters and grocery-store runs, he is an imposing figure. About six-and-a-half feet tall with a graying beard, a mohawk-style mullet, and draped in a black-and-white custom “Gambler 500” poncho, he looks as if Tyler Durden and Dax Shepard had a brother. Looks can be deceiving. Beneath Morgan’s burly exterior lurks a gentler side—at least, there must be. You don’t spend the good part of a decade turning an off-road rally for crappy cars into the most successful trash-collecting effort in the world if you don’t have a big heart. Gambler 500 founder Tate Morgan cruises Gambler Town sporting his custom poncho. Nick Jaynes Since 2018, the Gambler 500 and its sister organization, Sons of Smokey , have removed 5.5 million pounds of trash from public lands. “More than any other organization on the face of the planet,” Morgan says. If you’re surprised by that fact, so was I. Now in its tenth year, the Gambler 500, internationally infamous for hooliganism and outright bedlam, has changed a lot in the last decade. I attended the first three public Gambler 500 events, starting in 2017 (a few events beforehand were private, just Morgan and his friends). But I’d not been back since 2019. And I’d left the event with something of a sour taste in my mouth, certain that it had jumped the shark. Keen to reacquaint myself with the Gambler, my buddy Willy and I, accompanied by my dogs, Arlo and Rocco, loaded our camping gear into my ’76 International Scout Traveler , the Gamblin’est rig I have, and headed southeast from Portland toward Madras. Sugar High, Devil-Bound Nick Jaynes Nick Jaynes Nick Jaynes Due to a medication I am currently taking, I can’t consume dairy. It really throws off my milk-heavy breakfast diet. So, the Friday morning of the Gambler 500, I had half a bag of watermelon gummy candies and a cup of black coffee for breakfast—an embarrassing most important meal of the day for any self-respecting 41-year-old. On the Gambler, though, it felt oddly fitting. Cranked up on sugar and caffeine, I gleefully throttled the Traveler’s 345 V-8 up Oregon Highway 26, over Mt. Hood toward our first waypoint. Morgan offers three routes for Gamblers: “Madras Meander (short),” “Tumalo Pipeline (pop down to Bend and say hi),” and “The Devil’s Butthole (‘it’s a long way to the top if you wanna rock and roll’).” Willy and I chose to rock and roll. In years past, the highlight of the Gambler was the mob of wacky cars exploring Oregon’s backcountry and fire roads. These ostensibly $500 machines ostensibly covered 500 miles, but the routes were unofficial, so Morgan never really leaned into the specifics. In the event’s first few iterations, no matter which route you chose, you’d find it teeming with Gamblers ready to party. Nick Jaynes I’d run previous Gamblers with a group of friends, but this year it was just Willy and the dogs and me. We were certain we’d encounter a merry group of Gamblers on the way and make some fast friends. As we hung a left off Highway 97 out of La Pine toward Hole in the Ground, however, I had a realization: We hadn’t seen any other Gamblers since we passed through Madras 90 minutes ago. Around 6 o’clock that evening, 15 miles down the dirt two-track east of La Pine, the temperature began to drop. An unseasonable late-June cold front was settling in the area. Willy and I decided to set up camp and resume our Gambler search in the morning. Sons of Smokey Nick Jaynes Once we’d made camp, the dogs piled out of the truck and ran amok in the dirt after having been cooped up in the Traveler all day. Willy threw on some coats and thumbed open the Sons of Smokey app on a single bar of signal. It’s a free app that anyone can use, created in response to the myriad systems that private and public agencies and organizations were using for tracking illegally dumped garbage and abandoned vehicles. With it, anyone can tag the location of rubbish in need of removal on public land. You can add info like type of garbage, size, and how big a vehicle will be needed to remove it. And with the app, anyone can navigate to that site and snag it. This is the engine that drives the Gambler 500’s trash-collecting and disposal efforts each year. It’s no longer just hobbyists using the Sons of Smokey app, either. The Bureau of Land Management in Utah now uses it to manage dump sites across the land it oversees, and the Forest Service, which once eyed the Gambler warily, now sends rangers, Smokey Bear, and crews to work the cleanups alongside it. The app is free on iOS and Android, and getting it into more hands is the one thing Morgan asked me to pass along. He started Sons of Smokey informally back in 2017, but he didn’t formalize it as a 501(c)(3) until 2021, when Ford came knocking. The mission is narrow on purpose: get trash off public land—not just litter, but the abandoned cars, RVs, and boats that the Forest Service and BLM simply don’t have the staff or budget to haul out. Since 2018, Gambler 500 participants have removed 5.5 million pounds of trash from public lands, including hundreds of abandoned cars, boats, trailers, and motorhomes. Nick Jaynes For his part, Morgan refuses to put a single person on payroll, himself included. As he sees it, the moment you’re paying salaries, you’re no longer fundraising to clean up trash; you’re fundraising to make sure the staff keeps getting paid. He’d rather the gas-station clerk who buys a Sons of Smokey hat knows that his money goes straight to disposal fees, not to somebody’s Starbucks order. It’s the kind of stubbornness that makes for a lousy business plan and a hell of a nonprofit. So, the org stays deliberately lean: Individual donations and grants—like the Bronco Wild Fund money that covered much of last year’s haul—go almost entirely to the dump bill, which is the real expense. Corporate dollars come, too, but Morgan takes them warily, because they tend to arrive shrink-wrapped in marketing activations that are more about talking up the cleanup than actually doing it. There’s a philosophy underneath all of it, too. Tate Morgan has worked to keep the Gambler a big tent, pushing back on the flag-waving, macho strain of car culture he watched creep into the event’s early years. “I don’t wear my politics on my shoulder,” he told me. Picking up trash, the way he sees it, is something anyone who uses public land can get behind, regardless of who they voted for. It’s stewardship as common ground. Older and Wiser Nick Jaynes The Gambler 500 is always held Friday to Sunday during an early summer weekend in Central Oregon. The dates change from year to year, and so does the main event location. In 2017, the staging area, Gambler Town, was in the parking lot of Hoodoo Ski Area Mt., about 140 miles southeast of Portland. For 2018–19, Gambler Town was in a pumice pit outside of tiny Chemult. If the word “pumice” conjures images of dust clouds in your mind, you’re on the right track. Just take whatever you’re picturing and double it. This year, due to elevated drought-driven fire risk, Morgan intended to move the event from Madras toward Christmas Valley. “You can’t set sand on fire,” he says. But when word spread of the Gambler’s departure, Madras officials and the Forest Service asked Morgan to stay. The event is a windfall for whichever town hosts it; in the Chemult years, Morgan says, it brought an estimated $1.1 million in extra weekend spending to the local economy. The elevated fire risk of 1500 hoopties driving around the grasslands was worth the economic boon to the region. So, they gave Morgan the keys to the grass fields behind the Sheriff’s Office and increased Forest Service fire personnel for the weekend, including a helicopter. This year’s Gambler Town was smaller and more sedate than the last time I attended. That melee was more like “Mad Max” meets “Jackass” meets a pirate raid. Save the aforementioned throttle-happy CR-V–driving chucklehead, this was a quieter place than in years past. We Gamblers are 10 years older than we were during the first event, and that maturity was mostly reflected in the way the attendees comported themselves. Morgan admits that turnout isn’t what it was during the pumice-pit era, which peaked at 8000 attendees. “Year-over-year growth is the logic of cancer,” Morgan says, justifying the smaller numbers at Gambler Town with a shrug. Returning to Town Nick Jaynes Nick Jaynes Nick Jaynes On Saturday morning, Willy and I returned to the Devil’s Butthole track keen to find some Gamblers in the wild. By lunchtime, we had found none. We gave up the search, turned around, and headed north toward Gambler Town. We didn’t see any other Gamblers until just a few miles south of Madras—a stark contrast to past years, when the whole region was teeming with hoopties. We weren’t in Gambler Town more than a few minutes before Morgan rolled up to me on his scooter. It was as if his centurions at the gate alerted him to my arrival. I remarked how few Gamblers we saw outside of the Madras region. The majority of folks were out in the grasslands, collecting trash, he said. Willy and I stood near the front gates and watched as Gamblers returned to drop off the trash they’d collected during the day. It was a constant flow of lifted, straight-piped Panther-platform Fords and domestic economy hatchbacks with intentionally misspelled slogans and slurs scrawled across the bodywork in spray paint. The juxtaposition of what my eyes saw, a bunch of filthy hooligans in pirate cars, and what I knew they were doing, each unloading hundreds of pounds of trash they’d spent their weekend collecting on public land, almost made me lightheaded. What started in 2017 as a 500-mile off-road race for $500 cars culminating with a seething all-night party that would make the devil himself pray for earplugs had become a weekend-long exercise in improving public land, accented with a parade of slipshod jalopies. This Chevy Sprint with 1800cc Honda Goldwing power was the slipshoddiest of jalopies in all of Gambler Town. Nick Jaynes Ten years ago, Morgan unwittingly tapped into a vein of wanton destruction that had been dormant in Gen-Xers and millennials since Woodstock ’99. Over the last decade, he’s accomplished the impossible: Rather than use his Gambler army for evil—he could have very well become a Bane-like supervillain—he harnessed it for good. Following my last entry in the event, I publicly criticized the Gambler 500 (and, through transitive property, Tate Morgan) for losing the thread and becoming an excuse to sell merch. Attending this year was my way of finding out if I was right or wrong. So, is the Gambler 500 like it used to be? No, it’s not. It’s not as populated, and it’s not as raucous. From the ashes of the superficial original Gambler 500 has risen something much bigger, more important. The world has changed, too. Morgan admits there are no $500 cars anymore, and even being able to afford to buy and modify a crappy car for a weekend event is a luxury. So, he welcomes with open arms folks in their daily drivers, so long as they show up to the gates of Gambler Town with a shovel, a fire extinguisher, five gallons of water, and a load of trash. “You were the first and only person to ever be mean to me,” Morgan tells me. “Everyone else… I just get attaboys constantly. So, it was refreshing to have some hate.” For the record, Tate, it wasn’t hate: It was my misunderstanding. I didn’t quite see what you were up to. So, consider this a correction. What you have now built in Sons of Smokey and the Gambler 500 is truly impressive. I regret the error. The post A Gambler 500 Mea Culpa appeared first on Hagerty Media .

title: Is Cold Calling Dead in 2026? - Throxy
summary: Email is dying. Cold calling isn't. Here's what the data says about B2B outbound in 2026.
body_text: Is Cold Calling Dead in 2026? Why B2B Companies in Traditional Industries Are Picking Up the Phone Again There's a piece of received wisdom in B2B sales that's been repeated so often it's become gospel: cold calling is dead. LinkedIn thought leaders say it. Marketing blogs say it. Even some sales trainers say it. And every time someone repeats it, another company quietly pulls back from the phone, and another gap opens up for the companies that didn't. Here's the thing about consensus in outbound sales: when everyone agrees on something, the contrarians usually win. Why email-only B2B outbound is failing Email-only outbound is in trouble, and the data makes it hard to argue otherwise. Email-only campaign lead rates dropped 22.2% year-over-year. Microsoft Outlook's inbox placement crashed 26.7 percentage points in the same period. The cause isn't hard to diagnose: AI has made it trivially easy to flood every buyer's inbox with thousands of "personalised" emails that all read exactly the same way. Only 5% of senders genuinely personalise every email they send. Those senders see 2–3x better results than everyone else. The other 95% are sending noise and calling it an outbound sales strategy. Meanwhile, 73% of B2B buyers now actively avoid vendors who blast irrelevant outreach. Your emails aren't just being ignored. They're training your prospects to treat anything from your domain as spam. If your entire outbound strategy fits inside a spam folder, you don't have a strategy. You have a hope. B2B cold calling statistics that challenge the "dead" narrative While email deliverability collapses, something quietly remarkable is happening on the phone. 69% of B2B buyers still answer cold calls from new providers. 49% of buyers say they actually prefer initial contact by phone. And 57% of C-level executives and VPs prefer phone communication over email or social media when engaging with vendors. Across all 11 industries surveyed in HubSpot's research, phone calling ranks in the top three outbound channels. The explanation is simple supply and demand. Everyone fled to email because it felt scalable and safe. That mass migration left the phone channel less crowded than it's been in years. The companies still calling, and calling well, are operating in a wide-open lane while their competitors fight for attention in an inbox graveyard. The industry average cold calling success rate has climbed to 2.7% in 2026, up from 2.3% the year prior, with top-performing teams reaching success rates above 6%. Cold calling didn't die. Everyone just stopped doing it at the same time, and the companies that stayed picked up the slack. Why cold calling works for manufacturing, logistics, and healthcare This is where the conversation gets specific, and where generic SaaS outbound playbooks fall apart. If you sell into traditional industries like manufacturing, logistics, healthcare, or aerospace, your ICP isn't a startup founder scrolling their LinkedIn feed at 10am. They're an operations director on a shop floor. A procurement lead between supplier meetings. A hospital administrator who hasn't opened LinkedIn in three weeks. The "digital-first" outbound playbook was built by people selling to other people who live online. It wasn't designed for industries where decision-makers spend their day in physical environments, away from screens, reachable primarily by one channel: their phone. Ask your sales team a simple question: "How did our last five closed deals actually start?" If the answer is a phone call or an in-person meeting, your outbound strategy needs voice, and it needed it yesterday. The best windows to reach buyers in traditional industries? Early morning (7:30–9am) and late afternoon (4–5:30pm), before and after the operational day consumes their attention. Tuesdays tend to be the strongest day for connecting, while Mondays, when decision-makers are clearing the weekend backlog, are consistently the weakest. How to use voicemails as a B2B prospecting tool Here's a stat that should change how your SDR team thinks about unanswered calls: prospects who receive a voicemail before an email are 23% more likely to open that email. Most sales development reps treat voicemail as a failure state. The call didn't connect, so they hang up and move on. But that's dozens of missed opportunities every day, chances to leave a 20-second message that plants your name, your company, and a relevant insight directly on your prospect's phone. A voicemail isn't a failed call. It's a free 30-second ad placed exactly where your prospect will hear it. The companies getting this right follow a simple, repeatable pattern: Leave a short, industry-specific voicemail (20 seconds max, rehearsed, not scripted-sounding) Send a tailored email within 15 minutes that references the voicemail Repeat consistently across the week as part of a wider sequence No increase in call volume required. The voicemail warms the email. The email capitalises on the familiarity. The compound effect is what turns a stranger into someone the prospect has "seen around." When was the last time your team actually practised their voicemail script? If the answer is "never," you're leaving one of the most effective micro-touchpoints in B2B outbound completely to chance. Multichannel outbound: why cold calling alone isn't enough either To be clear: we're not arguing that cold calling alone is the answer. No single channel is. The power comes from combining them. Content builds familiarity. Email delivers the pitch. Phone creates urgency. LinkedIn adds credibility. Together, multichannel outbound sequences deliver up to 287% higher conversion than single-channel outreach. Yet most B2B companies are still running email-only. Consider the compound effect in practice: your prospect sees a LinkedIn post on Monday about a problem they recognise. Gets a cold email on Wednesday that references that exact problem. Doesn't reply. Gets a 20-second voicemail on Thursday. Opens the email that afternoon. By Friday, your SDR isn't a cold caller. They're someone the prospect has noticed three times in one week. That's the difference between interrupting someone's day and entering a conversation they've already started paying attention to. 82% of B2B buyers say individual thought leadership influences their purchasing decisions. Creator content is 4x more influential than company-produced marketing material. When your CEO or founder is posting consistently on LinkedIn, your SDR's cold calls land in a completely different context. "Oh yeah, I've seen your stuff" versus "Who are you and how did you get this number?" The companies treating outbound as a single-channel exercise in 2026 are at a structural disadvantage. Their prospects are using ten channels to research their next purchase. Matching that with one channel isn't a strategy. It's a limitation. "We tried outbound and it didn't work" is the most expensive misdiagnosis in B2B sales If you've said this sentence before, it's worth asking an uncomfortable question: did you test the channel, or did you test doing the channel badly? A rushed pilot with an unwarmed domain, a junior hire with no playbook, and no phone component doesn't test outbound. It tests neglect. And it's an expensive way to reach the wrong conclusion. Domain warming alone takes 4–6 weeks. SDR ramp averages 3–5 months. A meaningful outbound test, one that actually tells you whether the channel works for your business, needs at least five months of committed infrastructure and execution. The companies seeing real results from B2B cold calling aren't doing anything revolutionary. They're doing the basics with discipline. Proper infrastructure: warmed domains, verified data, authentication protocols. Trained reps: structured onboarding, call recordings, objection playbooks, and weekly coaching. Researched call lists: verified contacts matched to ICP, not bulk-scraped databases full of dead numbers. Practised voicemails: rehearsed, industry-specific, followed by coordinated emails. And multichannel sequences: phone, email, LinkedIn, and content working together, not in silos. Cold calling isn't dead. It's just being done badly by most people and well by the ones booking meetings you'll never hear about. The bottom line for B2B companies in traditional industries If your buyers aren't scrolling LinkedIn, if they work on factory floors and in hospitals and in procurement offices, the phone is your most direct line to a conversation. The companies that abandoned calling left a gap. The ones that fill it, with proper infrastructure, trained people, and multichannel coordination, are the ones building pipeline their competitors don't even know exists. The real question isn't whether cold calling works. It's whether you're willing to do it properly. Throxy builds outbound systems for B2B companies selling into traditional industries, including manufacturing, logistics, healthcare, aerospace, and industrial tech. If your buyers aren't online, we know how to reach them. Book a call: https://throxy.cal.com/gtm/strategy-call

title: US Defense Manufacturer, Elmet Technologies, to Streamline Supply Chain for Rapid Production of Hypersonic Vehicle Parts with 3D Systems DMP Flex 350 Triple
summary:
US Defense Manufacturer, Elmet Technologies, to Streamline Supply Chain for Rapid Production of Hypersonic Vehicle Parts with 3D Systems DMP Flex 350 Triple Elizabeth Piet Fri, 07/24/2026 - 18:13
Release Date
Monday, Jul 27, 2026 6:50 AM
  • Made advancements for C103 material with 3D Systems AIG Group
  • Expects fast qualification and certification of machines and materials
  • Focuses on a fast, streamlined domestic supply chain
     

ROCK HILL, South Carolina, July 27, 2026 – Today, 3D Systems (NYSE: DDD) announced that Elmet Technologies, a wholly owned subsidiary of The Elmet Group (Nasdaq: ELMT) (“Elmet”), is deploying the DMP Flex 350 Triple metal additive manufacturing machine (laser powder bed fusion) for the rapid production of advanced aerospace parts for hypersonic vehicles. Utilizing a high-performance C103 material, the Elmet team expects to rapidly qualify and certify the system to begin production in 2026. 

High-performance C103 Material

Elmet Technologies has spent the last 8 years with 3D Systems’ Application Innovation Group (AIG), a team of expert engineers who consult, guide and assist customers with advanced development of processes and materials. As part of this work the team developed processing parameters for C103 material specifically for this deployment.  C103 is a niobium-based alloy composed primarily of niobium with hafnium and titanium, designed for extreme high-temperature and aerospace applications.

“We collaborated with AIG on the parameter sets for the C103 material,” said Scott Ohm, R&D Manager, Elmet Technologies. “The work was done on an earlier 3D Systems metal 3D printer and we expect that prior research work will make it very easy to begin production on the DMP 350 Flex Triple.”

Selecting the DMP 350 Flex Triple

The DMP Flex 350 Triple supports a 350 x 350 x 350 mm build size, with 3 lasers for greater productivity. A best-in-class low oxygen environment maintains <25 ppm oxygen, typically ~0-6 ppm oxygen. This low oxygen (and other interstitial element) environment allows for exceptional powder reuse rates along with tight control of metal chemistry and superior surface finishes.

Elmet Technologies intends to use this system for the production of large heat exchangers for hypersonic vehicles. Elmet Technologies selected this advanced metal 3D printer for a number of reasons:

  • Very low oxygen content maintained within the system makes it a strong choice for very high-quality, consistent and repeatable parts production using refractory metals
  • The larger build size helps to meet the growing requirements of customers
  • The 3-laser system can enable large production volumes, quickly
  • It works with Elmet’s novel in-house materials
  • It is anticipated to enable fast qualification and certification

“This machine, material and process should achieve qualification within a couple of months,” said Ohm. “We anticipate NASA 6030 certification a few months after that. This is very fast and indicative of the quality of this entire solution, as well as confirmation of the sound business case for collaboration 3D Systems’ Aerospace and Defense experts to streamline the qualification and certification process.”

Direct Production of Monolithic Metal Parts

Metal 3D printing from 3D Systems enables the design and manufacture of higher performance heat transfer structures that are accurate, complex, and leak tight with less assembly, shorter lead times, reduced costs, higher yield, and better component reliability versus legacy processes like brazing. The use of Direct Metal Printing (DMP) reduces reliance on extended supply chains and helps protect intellectual property while delivering components that cannot be produced using traditional methods including thin walls, increased surface-to-volume ratios and maximal heat transfer with acceptable pressure drop.

“This collaboration with Elmet is a standout example of using metal additive manufacturing to create new advantages in aerospace design and production,” said Mike Shepard, Vice President of Aerospace & Defense, 3D Systems. “The low oxygen architecture of our DMP series metal additive machines is ideal for manufacture of complex components from highly reactive metals, like C103 and other refractory alloys.”

Securing the Supply Chain

By integrating in-house materials with 3D Systems’ DMP Flex 350 Triple, Elmet is working to secure its supply chain for the US defense industrial base, enabling fast, tool-free localized production of advanced aerospace parts. 

About 3D Systems

For 40 years Chuck Hull’s curiosity and desire to improve the way products were designed and manufactured gave birth to 3D printing, 3D Systems, and the additive manufacturing industry. Since then, that same spark continues to ignite the 3D Systems team as we work side-by-side with our customers to change the way industries innovate. As a full-service solutions partner, we deliver industry-leading 3D printing technologies, materials and software to high-value markets such as medical and dental; aerospace, space and defense; transportation and motorsports; AI infrastructure; and durable goods. Each application-specific solution is powered by the expertise and passion of our employees who endeavor to achieve our shared goal of Transforming Manufacturing for a Better Future. More information on the company is available at www.3dsystems.com.

title: High-Protein Meal Prep Ideas That Actually Keep You Full
summary: Discover high-protein meal prep ideas that keep you full by pairing 40g+ protein with 8g+ fiber, stabilizing blood sugar and stopping hunger for hours.
body_text: Why High-Protein Meal Preps Still Leave You Hungry Many busy professionals spend Sunday afternoon prepping plain chicken breast and white rice, only to find themselves reaching for snacks two hours after lunch. While protein is critical for muscle repair and metabolic health, relying on lean protein alone overlooks the physical mechanics of fullness. Without dietary fiber to add volume and slow digestion, even a 40g protein meal passes through the stomach quickly, causing sudden drops in satiety and energy. The Dual Mechanism of Satiety: Protein Plus Fiber To achieve lasting satiety, your digestive tract requires both macronutrient density and structural bulk. Quality protein triggers key gut satiety hormones, including glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and peptide YY (PYY) [1] , while dietary fiber delays gastric emptying. Fiber absorbs water and forms a viscous matrix in the gut, which prolongs nutrient absorption and maintains stable blood glucose levels across four to five hours. Protein stimulates cholecystokinin (CCK) and PYY release to signal fullness directly to the brain. Soluble and insoluble fiber expand in the digestive tract to slow gastric emptying and prevent rapid insulin spikes. Combined, 40-60g of protein and 8g+ of fiber keep appetite stable between meals, eliminating mid-afternoon energy crashes. Understanding this metabolic partnership changes how we design weekly meals. Grounding your routine in balanced nutrients ensures your body receives sustained energy rather than short-lived fullness. For an effective high-protein meal delivery strategy or home prep routine, pairing intact fiber sources with clean protein remains the non-negotiable foundation for daily performance. Four High-Protein, High-Fiber Meal Preps That Hold Up for Days When meal prepping for a four-day workweek, standard chicken and plain white rice often turn dry and leave you reaching for snacks by mid-afternoon. To build meals that stay fresh and keep you full until dinner, we pair 40 to 60g of quality protein with 8g or more of dietary fiber. Fiber slows gastric emptying and prolongs post-meal satiety, ensuring steady energy without blood sugar spikes [2] . By using high-moisture functional bases like bone broth-infused rice and cooking exclusively with heat-stable olive oil and avocado oil, these batch recipes maintain exceptional texture from Monday through Thursday. Edamame Noodle Steak Bowl: Combines sliced flank steak with edamame noodles and roasted broccolini, delivering over 45g of protein and 9g of fiber . Tossed in avocado oil and garlic, edamame noodles maintain a firm bite without absorbing excess moisture. Bone Broth Rice Chicken Plate: Features chicken breast served over rice infused with rich bone broth, paired with roasted carrots and dark leafy greens. Simmering rice in bone broth adds functional protein and prevents grains from drying out when reheated. Braised Beef Stew with Heirloom Beans: Pairs slow-cooked grass-fed beef with Rancho Gordo heirloom beans and kale for 50g+ of protein and 10g+ of fiber. Liquid-rich stews improve in depth of flavor by day three and four. Greek Yogurt Herb Chicken & Root Vegetables: Uses a Greek yogurt-based sauce with roasted root vegetables cooked in extra virgin olive oil. The yogurt base adds creamy protein while roasted root vegetables hold their structure for four full days. Every meal prep strategy must eliminate seed oils like canola, soybean, or sunflower oil, which oxidize easily and ruin fresh flavors. We rely strictly on pure extra virgin olive oil and avocado oil to protect nutritional value and taste. Building these habits at home ensures your high-protein and high-fiber meals support both immediate fullness and long-term vitality. Meal Prep Strategy: What to Batch Cook and What to Prep Fresh The biggest reason homemade meal prep fails by Thursday isn't a lack of discipline; it is texture degradation and food safety limits. According to official USDA cold storage guidelines, cooked meats and poultry keep safely in the refrigerator for 3 to 4 days [3] . Pushing cooked protein past day four compromises both taste and safety. To sustain a full week of high-protein eating, we recommend a split strategy: batch-cook durable foundation ingredients on Sunday, and spend two minutes assembling delicate components fresh each day. True satiety requires pairing 40–60g of protein with 8g+ of fiber per meal to slow gastric emptying and keep blood sugar steady. Maintaining this nutritional density without ending up with soggy, unappetizing meals comes down to dividing ingredients by their moisture tolerance. Batch cook (Days 1–4): Dense proteins like grilled flank steak or pasture-raised chicken thighs, paired with fiber-dense bases like bone broth-infused rice, edamame noodles, and roasted root vegetables . Prep fresh or assemble daily: Delicate greens like baby spinach, toasted pumpkin seeds, avocado, and Greek yogurt-based dressings or fresh chimichurri. Storage protocol: Pack cooked grains and meats into glass containers only after they cool completely to room temperature, preventing trapped steam from turning greens and roasted vegetables soggy. By keeping wet sauces and crisp produce separated in glass jars until lunchtime, your Thursday meal retains the same fresh texture as Monday's. For time-starved professionals, mastering this batch-and-separate method turns meal prep into a dependable system for lasting fullness and daily energy. The Clean Prepared Meal Shortcut for Demanding Weeks When demanding work schedules leave no room for four-hour Sunday prep sessions, maintaining strict nutritional standards often falls apart. For busy professionals in the SF Bay Area and Los Angeles, relying on standard restaurant takeout or mass-market prepared meals means settling for hidden seed oils, low protein ratios, and excess sodium. A clean meal delivery option provides a zero-friction alternative that preserves your health standards during high-intensity workweeks. 40 to 60g of quality protein per meal to meet daily anabolic and satiety needs. 8g+ fiber per meal to slow gastric emptying and eliminate post-meal hunger spikes [4] . No seed oils, cooking exclusively with extra virgin olive oil and avocado oil. Reusable, microplastic-free glass jars delivered directly to your doorstep. The Certified Clean High Protein Meal Subscription is built around complete ingredient transparency . Every batch undergoes independent third-party lab testing by Light Labs for heavy metals, pesticides, PFAS, and microplastics, with full lab results published online . Rather than spending hours shopping, cooking, and cleaning up, you receive fresh, nutrient-dense meals delivered every Monday across San Francisco, San Jose, and Los Angeles. Frequently asked questions Why do I feel hungry shortly after eating a high-protein meal? Protein stimulates fullness hormones like PYY and GLP-1, but lean protein eaten without adequate fiber digests rapidly. Without 8g or more of dietary fiber to slow gastric emptying and stabilize postprandial glucose levels, your stomach empties quickly, triggering hunger within two to three hours. How much fiber should I add to a high-protein meal prep? Aim for at least 8g of fiber per meal alongside 40 to 60g of protein. A landmark review published in The Lancet associated higher fiber intake with a 15 to 30% reduction in all-cause mortality, while practical fiber additions like roasted root vegetables or edamame noodles keep appetite stable throughout the afternoon. How long does high-protein meal prep stay safe in the fridge? According to USDA food safety guidelines, cooked meats, poultry, and fish remain safe in the refrigerator for 3 to 4 days at 40 degrees Fahrenheit or below. To ensure safety and preserve flavor, store meals in airtight containers or reusable glass packaging. What are the best ingredients for high-protein, high-fiber meal prep? Focus on durable proteins and complex, fiber-rich bases. Great options include grass-fed beef, pasture-raised chicken, edamame noodles, bone broth-infused rice, lentil salads, and roasted brassicas cooked in olive oil or avocado oil. Separate fresh greens and sauces until serving time. How can I maintain clean meal prep standards during busy work weeks? When time constraints make batch cooking difficult, look for prepared meal services that match strict kitchen standards. Locale delivers chef-crafted meals across the SF Bay Area and LA with 40 to 60g of protein, 8g+ fiber, zero seed oils, and published Light Labs testing in microplastic-free glass jars. title: New Swiffer Lemon Duster Delivers the Fresh Scent of Clean with No Spray Required
